native_mechanisms: A runner per road lays a stick on the far heap equal to the home ember plus that road's notch (edge relaxation nd = dist[u] + w).

One land-wide synchronized throw: every heap independently takes its own shortest sliver as its new ember, all other slivers burned, with no heap compared to any other heap (per-node local min, no global priority order).
A garrison seals a heap once its ember stops changing between throws, fixing its distance permanently and halting its runners.
core_technique: Frontier-based synchronized Bellman-Ford over CSR: dist held read-only for a whole round while per-node candidate minima accumulate (strict nd < dist && nd < cand test, SIMD gather-assisted), then all candidates committed at once and only changed nodes form the next frontier — hedged by an O(n^2) SIMD array-scan Dijkstra for dense/tiny graphs and a work-budget bailout to binary-heap Dijkstra.
